pr_comments: IMHO, the solution looks very suspicious. I understand that floats accuracy is not enough in some cases, but `+FLT_EPSILON` is a hack for this particular case, but not general solution.

@take1014, thank you for the contribution! can you please provide some explanation about the fix. If I understand correctly, with relatively big numbers the result will basically be the same (triangle area does not change if you shift all the vertices by the same amount), but with very small numbers by adding FLT_EPSILON you basically bring those coordinates to some "grid". But how effective is the fix? Why FLT_EPSILON is chosen for the shift, not 1 or even some variable that is computed out of the passed coordinates?

issue_context.title: Subdiv2D Insert Numerical Issue
issue_context.body:
### System Information

OpenCV 4.6.0
Python 3.8.15

### Detailed description

Inserting the points given below results in an
`error: (-201:Incorrect size of input array)  in function 'insert'`

The `locate` method is returning `PTLOC_ERROR`
I believe this is a numerical precision issue and the input should be handled without error.

https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blame/8b4fa2605e1155bbef0d906bb1f272ec06d7796e/modules/imgproc/src/subdivision2d.cpp#L419

https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blame/8b4fa2605e1155bbef0d906bb1f272ec06d7796e/modules/imgproc/src/subdivision2d.cpp#L276


### Steps to reproduce


```python
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
  
rect = (-5, -5, 10, 10)
subdiv = cv2.Subdiv2D(rect);

points = [
  (-1.18061450447522,2.22044604925031E-16),
  (0.199999999989984,1.38061450446519),
  (1.58061450445518,-2.22044604925031E-16),
  (-1.08061450447519,1.11022302462516E-16),
  (0.199999999989984,-1.28061450446519),
  (0.199999999989984,1.28061450446519),
  (1.48061450445516,-1.11022302462516E-16),
  (-1.18061450447522,0),
  (1.48061450445516,0),
  (-0.440307252242633,1.10904469332167),
];

(x, y) = np.reshape(points, (2, -1))
plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.scatter(x[-1], y[-1])
plt.show()

subdiv.insert(points)
```
Removing any point from the list will run correctly.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4276762/205152058-781b18e9-1249-4998-856f-b8e07cc879b2.png)


### Issue submission checklist

- [X] I report the issue, it's not a question
- [X] I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, forum.opencv.org, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found any solution
- [X] I updated to the latest OpenCV version and the issue is still there
- [X] There is reproducer code and related data files (videos, images, onnx, etc)
